title: Console: pivot to Minimal Telemetry Surface — scope reduction & acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: The original Console PRD proposed a broad telemetry surface: multiple dashboard cards (routes, models, user cohorts), full trace waterfall views, and a per-request token-level cost breakdown. After stakeholder reviews and capacity constraints (FE eng bandwidth + telemetry ingestion cost), we are intentionally cutting scope for the first MVP to focus on high-impact telemetry with the smallest implementation surface.

Decision summary: For MVP we will: 1) ship a single consolidated Costs & Health dashboard card set (top-level route-level cost/time aggregates), 2) provide lightweight sampled trace links (trace metadata + 1% sampled full trace storage) rather than full waterfall UI, and 3) postpone token-level per-request breakdown to a followup. The console will expose a route filter and 7-day/30-day windows; detailed per-model breakdown is deferred.

Why: Aligns with Redwood’s production-first goal — provide metrics that unblock cost debugging and route-level SLA assessment while keeping backend ingestion and FE complexity low. This reduces implementation risk and ongoing telemetry costs, enabling quicker release and iteration based on real usage.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Costs & Health dashboard card is visible to users with Console access and shows route-level aggregates (tokens, total spend, median latency) for the selected window (7d, 30d)
AC-2: Dashboard card load time is < 1.2s for typical accounts (<= 100k requests/day) and paginates when >20 routes

AC-3: Trace linking: every error or spike in latency on the dashboard includes a sampled trace link that opens a read-only trace page with span list and metadata — sample rate configurable but defaults to 1%
AC-4: Sampling storage cost must be forecasted and capped: projected additional monthly ingestion < $3k for pilot cohort; engineering to implement retention policies (30 days)
AC-5: Feature flags exist to toggle detailed trace collection and to enable token-level cost debugging (default off).
AC-6: PRD and rollout notes (Confluence doc) include migration path for customers who previously relied on token-level breakdown; support playbook drafted.
AC-7: Basic role gating: Console users without the billing role cannot view per-route spend; UI respects existing RBAC mappings.
AC-8: End-to-end acceptance test exists in CI that validates dashboard rendering with synthetic telemetry and verifies links to sampled traces work (mock backend).
changes_log: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Patel: Initial triage and draft PRD attached. Highlighted cost and FE bandwidth constraints.
2026-03-04 — Marco Reyes: Engineering feedback — full trace waterfall and token-level cost would add ~4 sprint infra work; proposed sampling + route-level as compromise.
2026-03-06 — Nina Zhou (SRE): Asked for retention/ingestion cap before approving sampling. Added requirement for 30-day retention and $3k ingestion cap.
2026-03-08 — Design review (Liam O’Neill): Provided low-fidelity mocks for single consolidated card and a lightweight trace modal; recommended deferring costly interactions (zoom, flamegraphs).
2026-03-10 — Product sync: Decision recorded to proceed with Minimal Telemetry Surface; created feature-flag tickets and assigned eng ownership.
comments: Marco Reyes (2026-03-04): Engineering note — we can reuse existing route-aggregation materialized view from billing service to avoid new ETL. Will prototype API surface this week.
Nina Zhou (2026-03-06): SRE — must include an emergency kill-switch for trace ingestion if customer cost spikes. Also require dashboard query timeouts to avoid SLO degradation.

Liam O’Neill (2026-03-08): Design q: can we get away with a single metric row per route plus a sparkline instead of full mini-charts? That saves FE rendering. Designers prefer sparklines + 3 key numbers.
Customer Success (2026-03-09): Some pilot customers requested token-level breakdown for cost investigations. We'll offer an experimental opt-in under a feature flag and document limits.
Aisha Patel (2026-03-10): PM decision — token-level breakdown moved to 'experimental' follow-up. Team to deliver minimal telemetry MVP for April release window.
